s: to land (to reach solid ground in an air, water or space vessel)
Das Flugzeug landet auf der Landebahn.
The plane lands on the runway.
to land (to make an air, water or space vessel reach solid ground)
Wir landen das Boot an diesem Strand.
We're landing the boat on this beach.
Nach vielen Missgeschicken bin ich hier gelandet.
After a lot of misadventures I ended up here.
Schon das erste Vogel-Fossil, 1861 entdeckt, landete über drei Ecken für 700 englische Pfund im Britischen Museum in London.
The very first bird fossil, discovered 1861, already ended up, through various intermediaries, in the British Museum for a price of 700 pounds.

land (part of Earth which is not covered by oceans or other bodies of water)
country, countryside (rural area, as opposed to a town or city)

s: Landau (an independent town in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany; official name: Landau in der Pfalz)
a town in Dingolfing-Landau district, Lower Bavaria region, Bavaria; official name: Landau an der Isar
Landau.et: From the common West Germanic element *land (“land, territory”) and *auwju (“floodplain”).

s: a chiefly Jewish surname transferred from the place name
Landau.et: From the common West Germanic element *land (“land, territory”) and *auwju (“floodplain”).

s: a (male) national; one who comes from some country or region
Siehst du das ausländische Auto da? Was ist denn das für ein Landsmann?
Do you see that foreign car? What country are they from?
a (male) compatriot; a fellow countryman; one who comes from the same country or region as another
Der Oppositionsführer hat seine Landsleute zum Widerstand aufgerufen.
The opposition leader has called his compatriots to resistance.
Es ist doch immer schön, wenn man sich mal mit einem rheinischen Landsmann unterhalten kann.
It’s always nice to have the chance to talk to a fellow Rhenish person once in a while.
Landstuhl (a town and municipality of Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany)
district (see Districts of Germany, which are called Landkreise in German)
Landshut (an independent town, the administrative seat of the Lower Bavaria region, Bavaria, Germany)
a rural district of the Lower Bavaria region, Bavaria, surrounding but not including the town of Landshut, which nevertheless serves as its administrative seat
Landau in der Pfalz (an independent city in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany)
farmer, agriculturist (male or of unspecified gender)
Landwirt.et: Land (“land”) + Wirt (“host; caretaker”). Chiefly a backformation from Landwirtschaft (“agriculture”).

s: Aus all' den glatten Weibergesichtern mach ich mir so viel als aus einem aufgedrieselten Taue. Ich wollte, wir stächen wieder in die See. Was sollen wir auch hier bei den verzweifelten Landratten!
Of all these smooth women's faces I make as much as of a feezed end of rope. I wish we would set out to sea again. What would we do here, with all these desperate landlubbers!
Jetzt lachten alle. „Ein Cyklonenritt!“ wiederholte der Kapitän. „Woher wissen denn Sie eingefleischte Landratte, der Sie nicht einmal „Seebeine“ besitzen, was das Ding bedeuten will?“
Now everybody laughed. "Riding a cyclone!", the captain repeated. "From where would you, a dyed-in-the-wool landlubber, not even having "sea legs", know what such a thing means?"
landlubber, landrat (someone unfamiliar with seamanship): Someone who dislikes being in or on the water.
land rat (rat living on land, as opposed to water rats)
Ihr Schwanz ist kleiner als an einer Landratte […]
Its tail is smaller than that of a land rat […]

Aber Schiffe sind nur Bretter, Matrosen sind nur Menschen; es gibt Landratten und Wasserratten, Wasserdiebe und Landdiebe—ich will sagen, Korsaren, und dann haben wir die Gefahr von Wind, Wellen und Klippen.
But ships are but boards, sailors but men; there be land rats and water rats, water thieves and land thieves, I mean pirates; and then there is the peril of waters, winds, and rocks.
Landratte.et: From Land (“land”) + Ratte (“rat”), probably formed as an antonym to Wasserratte. According to Duden, a 19th century calque of English landrat, though the earliest attestation seems to be slightly earlier, in a 1789 play by Kotzebue.

s: landscape: land as defined by its geographical (and architectural) features
Die Landschaft der Tundra ist von Moos, Gras und flachen Sträuchern geprägt.
The landscape of the tundra is dominated by moss, grass, and short shrubs.
landscape: scenery, land as viewed from a given vantage point
Vom Gipfel hat man einen wunderbaren Blick über die Landschaft.
From the mountain top you have a wonderful view of the landscape.
landscape: a picture, especially a painting, of such a view
Sein Spätwerk besteht hauptsächlich aus Landschaften.
His late oeuvre consists mostly of landscapes.
landscape: a scenario or social constellation with its various features and players
region, area, territory, chiefly one of historical or cultural (rather than political) relevance
Jede deutsche Landschaft hat ihren angestammten Dialekt, auch wenn er mancherorts fast ausgestorben ist.
Every German region has its inherited dialect, even if it has all but died out in some places.
Landschaft.et: From Middle High German lantschaft, from Old High German lantskaf. By surface analysis, Land + -schaft.

Landwirtschaft.et: From Land (“land”) + Wirtschaft (“householding, economy”). Also analysable as Landwirt (“farmer”) + -schaft (“-ship”).

s: landscaper, landscape gardener, (male or of unspecified gender) (one that does landscaping)
area, district, landscape (geographical region of lesser size, typically sparsely inhabitated)
In der nordkanadischen Wildnis, nahe dem Großen Sklavensee, liegt ein Landstrich, den die Ureinwohner Nechalacho nennen.
In the northern Canadian wilderness, close to the Great Slave Lake, there is an area that the native inhabitants call Nechalacho.
Landstrich.et: 17th century, from Land (“land”) + Strich (“stroke, stretch”). Compare Dutch streek (“region”).

chief administrative officer of a district
state capital, capital of a Bundesland
statewide, on the level of Bundesland
landesweit.et: From Land (“land, country, state”) + -es- + weit (“wide, far”).

Landtagswahl.et: Landtag (“parliament of a federal state”) + -s- + Wahl (“election”)

s: Landeshauptmann (male [also female] or of unspecified sex; cf. Herr / Frau Landeshauptmann)
Any member in the suborder Oniscidea; a woodlouse

Any of the final reserves of the armed forces in Prussia and later Germany, in Austria, or in Switzerland, generally made up of older people, sometimes constituted as a regular portion of the country's armed forces, sometimes irregular.
a severe flood; a storm tide
Doch das nächste „Land unter“ kommt bestimmt.
But the next severe flood is definitely coming.
Ein paar Nordweststürme, hoch auflaufendes Wasser, läuft ja sowieso höher auf nach dem Eindeichen der halben Bucht, dann ist Land unter, es könnte zumindest sein.
A couple of nor'westers, high-rising water, which of course rises even higher after the damming of the bay, and then it's catastrophic flooding at minimum.
a situation where one is swamped with work
»Bei denen ist Land unter. Es wird ein paar Tage dauern.«
"They're absolutely swamped with work. It'll take a couple of days."
a town in the Upper Bavaria region, Bavaria; official name: Landsberg am Lech
a rural district of the Upper Bavaria region, Bavaria; official name: Landkreis Landsberg am Lech
a town in Saalekreis district, Saxony-Anhalt, near Halle; official name: Stadt Landsberg
simple regional wine; country wine, vin de pays
lansquenet (German mercenary of the 15th or 16th century)
a students' association of such kind (many of which exist in traditional university cities in German-speaking Europe)

The Corps Guestphalia is a Westphalian students' association in Bonn.
an association in Germany of Germans expelled from Germany's former eastern territories

Landmann.et: From Old High German lantman, equivalent to Land + Mann.

landlos.et: From Middle High German lantlōs, equivalent to Land + -los.

s: Landfriede; a peace between territorial rulers of the Holy Roman Empire
